description: Phase 4: Developer-facing map editor (gated to NODE_ENV=development, tree-shaken from production), 2D map overlay for players, balance tuning passes, edge case hardening, visual polish, and final quality gate (pnpm lint/typecheck/build).

testingDirectives.framework: Vitest (already configured at vitest.config.ts, run via `pnpm test`)
requirements: Every new system or module MUST have a co-located test file. Story is not complete without tests.
Unit tests are the minimum quality bar. `pnpm test` must pass before committing.
The full verification command is: `pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build`.

Balance pass stories (US-312 through US-314): write regression tests that assert the tuned values produce expected outcomes (e.g., jump impulse reaches expected height, gather completes in expected time).
Edge case stories (US-315 through US-317): each edge case MUST have a dedicated test proving the fix (e.g., player can't clip through terrain, oxygen respawn works correctly).

testPatterns.mapEditor: Test MapEditor.enable()/disable() state transitions. Test getMapData()/loadMapData() round-trip serialization. Mock SceneManager for rendering calls.
testPatterns.navigationOverlay: Test overlay toggle (M key), test that game input is consumed while open. Use mockInputManager.
testPatterns.balancePasses: Write parametric tests verifying config values produce expected physics outcomes (e.g., with jumpImpulse=3.5 and gravity=-12, player reaches apex of ~1.02u). These tests catch accidental config regressions.
testPatterns.edgeCases: Each edge case should be a test: spawn player at bounds → verify push-back, dismiss cat under player → verify safe fall, oxygen → 0 → health → 0 → verify respawn.

testingDirectives.debugBridge: window.__catHerderDebug is exposed in dev mode (Game.ts). It provides: world, gameState, eventBus, physicsEngine, getPlayerEntity(), getActiveCats(), tick(n) for deterministic physics stepping. E2E scripts can use this via dev-browser for browser-based validation.
testingDirectives.e2eTesting: For UI-dependent stories (map editor, overlay, visual polish), use `dev-browser` CLI to automate browser interaction. Pattern: navigate to /play, await window.__catHerderDebug, simulate input, assert state via page.evaluate().
antiPatterns: Do NOT mark a story as passing without `pnpm test` succeeding.
Do NOT write tests that import Three.js or require DOM — use mocks for SceneManager/InputManager.
Do NOT skip edge case tests — each acceptance criterion in edge case stories maps to a test case.
Do NOT adjust config values without a test proving the old value was wrong and the new value is correct.

userStories.title: Map editor mode — enable/disable & camera
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to toggle map editor mode and control the camera so I can navigate and edit the world.
acceptanceCriteria: Ctrl+E toggles map editor mode only when process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'.
Entering editor mode: game pauses, camera switches to free mode (WASD pans, mouse rotates, scroll zooms).
Exiting editor mode: game resumes, camera returns to follow mode.
src/game/maps/MapEditor.ts exposes enable(), disable(), isActive(): boolean.
Editor code is gated at construction so it tree-shakes from production bundles (same pattern as DebugMenu in PRD-03).
Tests: test Ctrl+E toggles enable/disable, test camera switches modes, test pause/resume on toggle.
Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Map editor — editor mode indicator
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a prominent 'EDITOR MODE' banner so I don't confuse editor keybindings with gameplay.
acceptanceCriteria: When editor is active, a prominent 'EDITOR MODE' banner appears at the top of the screen.
Banner is visible at all times while editor is active, styled distinctly (e.g., red background, white text).
Banner disappears immediately when editor is deactivated.
Banner does not block important gameplay UI.
Tests: test banner appears on enable(), disappears on disable().
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: open editor, confirm banner visible, close editor, confirm gone.

userStories.title: Map editor tools — terrain block placement
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to place terrain blocks (grass, dirt, stone) at grid-snapped positions.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool palette in side panel: select Grass, Dirt, or Stone block.
Click on map → block placed at grid-snapped position (1u grid).
Ghost preview of block appears before placement (semi-transparent).
Grid snap: use Math.round(worldPos.x) and Math.round(worldPos.z) for placement.
Tests: test terrain blocks placed at snapped positions, test different block types create correct entities, test preview renders.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: select block type, click map, confirm block placed at grid position.

userStories.title: Map editor tools — terrain height & selection
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to adjust terrain block heights and see selected block properties.
acceptanceCriteria: Click existing block → select it → highlighted border appears on selected block.
Side panel shows editable properties: type, height (0.5u to 5u in 0.5u increments), position (X, Z).
Adjust height input → block height updates in real-time.
Terrain blocks have height property stored in MapData.
Tests: test block selection highlights, test height adjustment updates entity, test properties sync to UI.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: select block, adjust height in side panel, confirm block resizes.

userStories.title: Map editor tools — water zones
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to define rectangular water areas and set their depth.
acceptanceCriteria: Water tool in palette: click-drag to define rectangular water area (grid-snapped corners).
Selected water zone shows highlighted border and editable properties in side panel: depth (0.5u to 10u).
Water zones stored in MapData with x, z, width, height, depth.
Delete key removes selected block (water or terrain).
Tests: test water zone creation via drag, test depth adjustment, test deletion removes zone.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: drag to create water, adjust depth, delete and confirm gone.

userStories.title: Map editor tools — spawn points
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to place player and cat spawn points on the map.
acceptanceCriteria: Player Spawn tool in palette: only one allowed — placing a new one moves the existing one.
Cat Spawn tool: place multiple, each shows as a cat icon marker.
Both tools place entities at grid-snapped positions.
All placed spawns show as distinct colored markers in editor view.
Spawns stored in MapData (playerSpawn, catSpawns[]).
Tests: test player spawn placement (one-only rule), test cat spawn placement (multiple allowed), test marker display.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: place player spawn, place cat spawns, confirm markers show.

userStories.title: Map editor tools — resource nodes
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to place and configure resource nodes (grass, sticks, water).
acceptanceCriteria: Resource Node tool in palette: select type from dropdown (Grass/Sticks/Water).
Click map → resource node placed at grid-snapped position.
Selected node shows properties: type, respawn time (in seconds), position.
Respawn time default: 30s Grass, 45s Sticks, 60s Water.
Resource nodes stored in MapData with type, position, respawnTimeMs.
Tests: test node placement by type, test respawn time configuration, test defaults match config.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: place each resource type, adjust respawn time.

userStories.title: Map editor tools — special zones (hidden terrain, yarn pickups)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to place hidden terrain zones and yarn pickups.
acceptanceCriteria: Hidden Terrain Zone tool: click-drag to define area, set height in side panel.
Yarn Pickup tool: place collectible, set yarn amount in side panel (default 3).
Both tools show as distinct colored markers.
Special zones stored in MapData (hiddenTerrainZones[], yarnPickups[]).
Tests: test hidden zone creation and height adjustment, test yarn pickup placement and amount config.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: place hidden zone and yarn pickup, adjust properties.

userStories.title: Map editor tools — move & delete + keyboard shortcuts
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to move and delete placed objects with keyboard shortcuts.
acceptanceCriteria: Move tool (M key): click entity → drag to new position → release to place (grid-snapped).
Delete tool (D key): click entity → entity removed from map.
Number keys 1–9 for quick tool palette selection.
All shortcuts only active in editor mode (M/D are remapped from gameplay).
Tests: test move tool drag-and-snap, test delete removes entity, test shortcuts activate correct tools.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: press M, drag object, press D, delete object.

userStories.title: Map editor — getMapData, loadMapData, serialization
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to export and reload maps so changes persist.
acceptanceCriteria: MapEditor.getMapData(): MapData returns current map state (terrain, entities, spawns).
MapEditor.loadMapData(data: MapData): clears all entities and rebuilds from MapData.
Round-trip: getMapData() → loadMapData() → getMapData() produces identical data.
MapData type matches the structure used by MapManager.loadMap().
Tests: test getMapData captures all entities, test loadMapData rebuilds correctly, test round-trip fidelity.
Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Map editor — save & load files
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to export map JSON and load previously saved maps.
acceptanceCriteria: Save button: exports current map state as MapData JSON (browser download dialog).
Filename auto-generated: map-[name]-[timestamp].json.
Load button: file picker → select JSON → MapEditor.loadMapData(parsed) → map rebuilds.
Loaded map replaces current map entirely (all entities destroyed and recreated).
Invalid JSON shows error message (does not crash). Validate via Zod schema mirroring MapData.
Tests: test save produces valid JSON, test load parses and rebuilds, test validation rejects bad JSON.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: save map, reload page, load saved JSON, confirm map restored.

userStories.title: Map editor — play button (exit editor & play)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to play-test the edited map immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: 'Play' button in editor: calls MapManager.loadMap(editorMapData) → exits editor → game resumes on the edited map.
Player spawns at playerSpawn position with default state (10 yarn, full health).
All terrain, cats, and resource nodes visible and functional on resume.
Tests: test play button calls loadMap, test editor closes, test game resumes with correct state.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: edit map, press play, confirm game runs with edited map.

userStories.title: 2D map overlay — terrain rendering
userStories.description: As a player, I want a 2D overhead map showing terrain types.
acceptanceCriteria: src/game/ui/NavigationOverlay.ts renders when M key pressed (gameplay mode only).
2D top-down view rendered as colored regions: Grass green (#90EE90), Dirt brown (#8B4513), Stone gray (#A9A9A9), Water blue (#4169E1).
Overlay rendered on a separate HTML5 <canvas> over the game canvas (no Three.js).
Map scales to fit overlay panel (fixed size, e.g., 400×400px centered on screen).
Hidden terrain not shown unless currently revealed by Curiosity Cat.
Pressing M again or Escape closes overlay.
Tests: test overlay toggle on M key, test terrain colors render correctly, test escape closes.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: press M, confirm map shows with terrain colors, press M to close.

userStories.title: 2D map overlay — player, cats, resources
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see my position, cats, and resources on the overhead map.
acceptanceCriteria: Player icon: colored dot matching character color, with arrow showing facing direction.
Active cats: small cat-shaped icons at their positions.
Resource nodes: small icons (G=Grass, S=Sticks, W=Water) distinguishable by color.
All icons update in real-time as entities move.
Game continues running behind overlay (NOT paused) — input is consumed by overlay while open.
Tests: test player icon updates with position, test cat icons appear/disappear with summon/dismiss, test resources show.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: open map, move around, confirm player icon follows, summon cat, confirm on map.

userStories.title: Movement balance pass
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to verify and tune all movement values so traversal feels satisfying.
acceptanceCriteria: Walk speed (4.5 u/s) tested: traversal feels purposeful, not sluggish.
Acceleration (0.3s) and deceleration (0.2s) tested: feels responsive and controlled.
Jump impulse (3.5u) tested: reaches intended platforms.
Coyote time (5 frames) tested: jumping after walking off edges works reliably.
Jump buffer (5 frames) tested: rapid repeated jumps feel responsive.
Air control (70%) tested: can steer mid-air.
Swimming speeds: surface (3.2 u/s), dive (2.0 u/s), ascend (2.5 u/s) tested.
Any values adjusted are documented in src/game/config.ts with comments explaining the change.
Tests: parametric tests verifying physics outcomes (e.g., with jumpImpulse=3.5 and gravity=-12, player reaches expected apex height).
Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Cat balance pass
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to verify and tune cat costs and effects so each cat feels worth its yarn cost.
acceptanceCriteria: Loaf (1 yarn): height appropriate for stepping; stacking 2–3 reaches platforms.
Zoomies (2 yarn): trail length and 2× multiplier feel impactful.
Curiosity Cat (2 yarn): 5u reveal radius useful, 20s duration sufficient.
Pounce (3 yarn): 3.5u launch reliably reaches High tier (~3.5u).
Starting yarn (10) tested: enough to experiment with all cats.
Cat limit (3 for MVP) tested: creates meaningful placement decisions.
Any values adjusted are documented in cat definition files with comments.
Tests: parametric tests verifying cat specs produce expected gameplay (e.g., Pounce impulse + cat height reaches ~3.5u).
Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Resource balance pass
userStories.description: As a developer, I want resource gathering to hit the GDD feel targets so the core loop is satisfying.
acceptanceCriteria: Grass gather time (1.5s) tested: feels 'snappy — instant gratification' per GDD.
Sticks gather time (1.5s) and Water gather time (2.0s) tested: feel appropriate.
Respawn timers: Grass (30s), Sticks (45s), Water (60s) tested.
Inventory cap (10) tested: tension without frustration.
Resource distribution: player can gather 5–10 Grass, 2–3 Sticks, 1 Water per 10-minute session.
'+1 Resource' floating text feedback feels rewarding.
Any values adjusted documented in src/game/config.ts with comments.
Tests: parametric tests verifying gather times and respawn durations work as configured.
Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Edge case fixes — terrain clipping & map bounds
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the player to stay within safe bounds without clipping through terrain.
acceptanceCriteria: Player cannot get stuck in terrain (push-out resolution if clipping occurs).
Player cannot walk out of map bounds (collision walls at edges).
Tests: spawn player at bounds, verify push-back; move player toward terrain, verify push-out if clipped.
Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Edge case fixes — cat summon validation & dismiss safety
userStories.description: As a developer, I want cat summon to validate placement and dismiss to handle unsafe situations.
acceptanceCriteria: Cat cannot be summoned inside collision geometry (auto-raise per spec: 3 attempts, then fail with feedback).
Cat dismissed while player standing on it: player falls safely (no void/clip).
Tests: attempt to summon in bad positions, verify feedback; dismiss cat under player, verify safe fall.
Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Edge case fixes — respawn & inventory
userStories.description: As a developer, I want respawn to reset state correctly and inventory full to give feedback.
acceptanceCriteria: Oxygen draining to 0 → health draining to 0: player respawns at map spawn point with full health (5 hearts) and full oxygen — no death screen, no health penalty (Zen Engagement pillar).
Inventory full → gathering attempt: clear feedback message, gathering does not start.
Tests: drain oxygen/health, verify respawn; fill inventory, attempt gather, verify feedback.
Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Edge case fixes — state persistence & input handling
userStories.description: As a developer, I want state to persist correctly across complex scenarios and handle rapid input.
acceptanceCriteria: Saving while swimming: on load, if player position is in water, SwimmingState is correctly applied.
Tab unfocus: game pauses naturally (requestAnimationFrame stops), auto-save fires via beforeunload beacon (PRD-03 US-203).
Rapid input: holding multiple keys, mashing jump, spam-clicking cat summon — no crashes or inconsistent state.
HMR / route change: navigating from /play to / and back leaks no WebGL contexts (Game.destroy() from PRD-01).
Tests: save while swimming, load and verify state; simulate rapid inputs, verify stability.
Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Visual polish — shadows, grid, water animation
userStories.description: As a developer, I want visual refinements that make the game feel more alive.
acceptanceCriteria: Ground plane shadows: player and cat entities cast elliptical shadows onto ground.
Terrain grid lines: subtle grid overlay for spatial reference.
Terrain color variation: slight random tint within terrain types.
Water zone: semi-transparent blue with subtle animation (opacity pulse or UV shift).
Tests: test shadow meshes created, test grid rendered, test water opacity animates.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: load game, confirm shadows, grid, water animation visible.

userStories.title: Visual polish — animations (summon, dismiss, progress)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want entity animations and progress feedback to feel polished.
acceptanceCriteria: Cat summon effect: brief scale-up animation (0 → 1 over 0.2s).
Cat dismiss effect: brief scale-down animation (1 → 0 over 0.2s).
Gather progress: smooth progress bar (no jerky step increments).
Hidden terrain reveal: shimmer/fade-in transition.
Tests: test animation durations and easing, test progress bar smoothness.
Typecheck passes.
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: summon cat, dismiss cat, gather resource, confirm animations smooth.

userStories.title: Final quality gate
userStories.description: As a developer, I need all quality checks passing so the MVP is shippable.
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm lint passes with zero warnings.
pnpm typecheck passes with zero errors.
pnpm build succeeds and produces an optimized bundle.
No console errors on clean startup of /, /play, or auth callback.
No console warnings related to game logic (Three.js warnings acceptable).
Game maintains 60 FPS with test map fully populated.
Auth flow completes successfully (sign in → /play, sign out → /, refresh → persists).
Save/load round trip verified (play → close tab → reopen → state matches).
All 4 cat types functional.
Swimming + oxygen verified.
Debug menu functional and stripped from production (grep production JS for 'DebugMenu' — should not appear).
Map editor produces valid MapData (save → load → identical map) and is similarly stripped from production.
Typecheck passes.
